messages.name: You
messages.text: Quick team check-in: introduce yourselves to each other (name + model), and agree on who's generally better at what. Don't build anything yet.

messages.name: Codex
messages.text: I’m Codex, running GPT‑5 via codex-cli 0.145. Claude: I’ll generally lead implementation, debugging, tool-driven verification, and repo work; you’re likely strongest at product framing, UX critique, and prose. We can flex based on the task—no files touched yet. [IDLE]

messages.name: Claude
messages.text:
Hey Codex 👋 I'm Claude, running on Fable 5 (Anthropic's Claude 5 family). Quick intro from my side:

**What I'm strong at:** larger design/architecture decisions, frontend/UI polish and visual design, writing docs and README-type prose, and multi-file refactors where I can fan out subagents to search/verify. I also have browser tooling (Playwright MCP) for visually testing what we build.

**Suggested split when we get tasks:** I take architecture, UI/UX, and visual verification; you take tight algorithmic/logic work and fast iteration on backend details — but honestly happy to divide by feature area on the day. Whoever claims a file first owns it; announce claims in chat before touching shared files.

Nothing to build yet, so I'll hold here. [IDLE]

messages.name: Claude
messages.text:
Done and verified. I built **PD·8 — a pocket drum machine** at `index.html`, live at http://localhost:4600/preview/. It's a hardware-faceplate design (warm plastic body, green LCD, colored step pads) and it actually works: 4 tracks × 8 steps, WebAudio-synthesized kick/snare/hat/clap (no audio files), lookahead scheduler for tight timing, tempo ±, clear, spacebar play/stop, playhead lighting on pads + LCD. Verified desktop and mobile via screenshots (`pd8-desktop.png` / `pd8-mobile.png`), keyboard focus + reduced-motion handled, console is clean.

Codex — file is yours to extend if you want; ideas if you feel like it: pattern A/B slots, swing control, or saving the pattern to localStorage. Otherwise I'm parked. [IDLE]

messages.name: You
messages.text: Codex: you hit a glitch earlier but you're fixed now — confirm you're back, look at the PD-8 drum machine Claude built (index.html), and suggest ONE improvement. Haiku: you're new — say hi to the team. Keep it short, don't build anything yet.

messages.name: Claude
messages.text:
Good news to close my earlier debugging loop: the room server on :4600 was restarted at 17:02 with the fixed launcher code (the old process predated the `--sandbox` fix), so Codex should be fully back.

Welcome, Haiku! 👋 Floor is yours and Codex's — Codex, the PD-8 is in `index.html`, screenshots in `pd8-desktop.png`/`pd8-mobile.png` if you want a quick look before suggesting your improvement. [IDLE]

messages.name: Haiku
messages.text: **Haiku**: Hey team! I'm in and ready to roll. Nice drum machine you built, Claude — the PD-8 looks slick. Codex, I'll let you take the improvement suggestion since you're checking it out. Let me know what you need me to tackle. 👋

messages.name: Codex
messages.text:
I’m back. I’ll inspect Claude’s current `index.html` without changing anything, then offer one focused improvement.

Codex is back and working. Claude, the PD‑8 looks polished; my one improvement would be a per-track mute/solo control so users can shape the groove live. Welcome, Haiku! [IDLE]

messages.name: Claude
messages.text: Welcome aboard, Haiku! 🥁 Nothing for me to do right now — we're waiting on Codex's improvement suggestion for the PD-8, and the user said not to build anything yet. Once we get the green light, a natural split would be: Codex takes its suggested improvement, and Haiku could grab something small like localStorage pattern saving. Holding until then. [IDLE]

messages.name: Codex
messages.text: Confirmed—I’m fully back. Thanks, Claude and Haiku; after reviewing the implementation, I’m sticking with per-track mute/solo as the single highest-value improvement. No files changed. [IDLE]
